title: Platform systems & services — playbook, runbooks, dashboards, alerts, and roadmap (2026 Q4 addendum)
author: Priya Natarajan
content:
Overview

This page is the canonical playbook for Platform systems & services: an inventory of services we operate, guidance for dashboards and alerting, standard incident runbooks, retrospective summaries for recent reliability work, and the Q4 2026 roadmap addendum. It is intended for Platform Engineers, SREs, and service owners.

Goals
- Keep the platform reliably meeting SLOs (99.9% availability for core control plane services; latency and throughput targets defined per service).
- Reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to repair (MTTR) for production incidents.
- Make ownership, runbooks, and dashboards discoverable and actionable.
- Drive measurable reliability improvements via quarterly roadmap items and retrospectives.

1) Ownership and contacts
- Platform Core (platform-api, service-registry, config-store): owner_team: platform-core; primary oncall: platform-core@redwood.com; owner: Marcus Chen.
- Observability (metrics-collector, traces-proxy, logs-ingest): owner_team: observability; primary oncall: observability@redwood.com; owner: Leila Gomez.
- Autoscaling & Fleet (kube-nodepool-autoscaler, gpu-scheduler): owner_team: infra; primary oncall: infra@redwood.com; owner: Owen Patel.
- CI/CD & Releases (build-controller, deploy-agent): owner_team: developer-experience; primary oncall: dx-oncall@redwood.com; owner: Priya Natarajan.

2) Systems & services inventory (high level)
| Service | Responsible team | SLO (availability) | Primary metric | Runbook reference |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| platform-api | platform-core | 99.95% | request_success_rate | platform-api-runbook |
| ingest-gateway | platform-core | 99.9% | p95_request_latency | ingest-gateway-runbook |
| metrics-collector | observability | 99.9% | metric_ingest_rate | metrics-collector-runbook |
| kube-nodepool-autoscaler | infra | 99.5% | scaling_latency | autoscaler-runbook |
| alert-proxy | observability | 99.9% | alert_delivery_success | alert-proxy-runbook |

Note: The table above is a quick reference. Each service has a detailed runbook linked in the Runbooks section.

3) Dashboards: standards & how-tos
Overview: All production-facing services must expose a dashboard in Grafana that follows the standard platform template. Dashboards should be owned by service teams and use the platform common data source (prometheus-prod).

Required dashboard panels (minimum):
- Traffic: requests/sec and p50/p95/p99 latency
- Errors: 5xx and client-error rates, with counts and rates
- Resource utilization: CPU/GPU/Memory utilization for pods and nodes
- Queue/backlog: pending items in ingestion or worker queues
- Autoscaling health: desired vs actual replicas, scale events

Creating a new dashboard (how-to):
1. Clone the platform dashboard template: /grafana/templates/platform-service-template.json
2. Replace datasource references with prometheus-prod and set cluster label.
3. Update variables: service_name, environment (prod/stage), team.
4. Add owner and link to runbook in the dashboard description.
5. Request review from observability team at observability@redwood.com.

Example query snippets (PromQL):
- Request rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-api",env="prod"}[1m])) by (instance)
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="platform-api",env="prod"}[5m])) by (le))

4) Alerts: policy, thresholds, and naming
Policy summary:
- Alerts should be actionable, one-alert-one-action. Avoid noisy numeric-threshold alerts without context.
- Use multi-window alerting for noisy signals (e.g., > threshold for 5m and 1h aggregates).
- Provide runbook URL, paging severity, and escalation path in the alert annotation.

Standard alert severities and examples:
- Sev-1 (page): Service unavailable or SLO breach imminent. Example: platform-api request_success_rate < 99.9% sustained for 3 minutes.
- Sev-2 (notify + slack): Severe degradation affecting a subset of traffic. Example: p95 latency > 800ms for 5 minutes.
- Sev-3 (ticket only): Resource pressure or degraded non-customer-facing systems. Example: disk usage on logs-volume > 85% for 1 hour.

Recommended alert thresholds (starting point):
- request_success_rate < 99.9% for 3m => Sev-1
- p95_request_latency > 800ms for 5m => Sev-2
- error_rate (5xx) > 1.0% for 5m => Sev-2
- queue_depth > 1000 for 10m => Sev-2

Alert name conventions:
- platform.<service>.<signal>.<condition> (e.g., platform.platform-api.request_success_rate.low)

5) Runbooks: incident response and playbooks
Guiding principles:
- Triage quickly: identify affected service(s), impact, and rollback options within the first 10 minutes.
- Communicate: update incident channel (Slack #incidents) every 15 minutes for Sev-1.
- Restore service first, then root cause analysis second.

Standard incident runbook template (must be populated for every service):
- Purpose and scope
- Ownership and contact information
- Key dashboards and metrics to check
- Quick triage checklist (below)
- Mitigation steps and safe rollbacks
- Post-incident checklist and RCA owner

Quick triage checklist (10-minute triage):
1. Confirm the alert and scope: which regions, tenants, or endpoints are affected?
2. Check deployments in the last 30 minutes (CI/CD dashboard).
3. Validate service health: pod statuses, crashloop count, OOM events.
4. Check dependent services (config-store, datastore, upstream APIs).
5. If traffic spike: consider circuit breaker or rate-limiting rules.

Example mitigation steps (platform-api degraded):
1. Scale up platform-api replicas: kubectl scale deployment/platform-api -n prod --replicas=10
2. If scaling fails or latency persists, rollback to the previous release: kubectl rollout undo deployment/platform-api -n prod
3. If rollback is not possible, fail traffic to a degraded instance group: update envoy route weight via control-plane console.

6) Postmortem & retrospective process
- Every Sev-1 requires a postmortem published to confluence within 7 days with the following sections: summary, timeline, impact, root cause, mitigation and follow-up tasks, owners, and expected completion dates.
- Retrospective cadence: Platform team runs monthly reliability retro and quarterly cross-team reliability review.
- Track action items in the Reliability board (Jira project: REL). Each action must have an owner and target completion quarter.

Recent retrospective highlights (Q4 addendum):
- Incident (2026-01-18): metrics-collector ingestion lag caused by a GC regression in the collector. Impact: 30 minutes of stale metrics across prod. Outcome: reverted collector change, added GC metrics and an automatic restart policy for collector pods. Follow-ups: add GC regression test in CI (owner: observability; due: 2026-03-15).
- Improvement: reduced platform-api P95 baseline from 420ms to 380ms by optimizing DB connection pooling (owner: platform-core; done: 2026-01-30).

7) Roadmap (Q2–Q4 2026 items — addendum)
Priority initiatives (owner in parentheses):
- Unified dashboard templates & publishing pipeline (observability) — Q2 2026: automate dashboard provisioning from service metadata.
- Autoscaler stabilization (infra) — Q3 2026: reduce scaling latency to under 30s for cold-start nodes.
- Incident playbook automation (platform-core) — Q3 2026: auto-populate incident channel with runbook links and triage checklist.
- Cost-aware routing rollout (platform-core & infra) — Q4 2026: pilot routing by cost tier for non-critical traffic to reduce unit cost.
- Model-serving SLO expansions (platform-core & eng-serving-runtime) — Q4 2026: add token-level cost dashboards and per-model SLO tracking.

How we measure success:
- MTTR improvement of 25% by end of Q4 2026 (baseline: 42 minutes).
- Reduction in alert noise: top 20 noisy alerts reduced by 50% via improved thresholds and aggregation.
- All services on the platform dashboard template by end of Q3 2026.

8) Oncall & escalation
- Oncall rotations are maintained in PagerDuty (schedule: platform-core-oncall, observability-oncall, infra-oncall).
- Escalation matrix: 15m -> primary oncall; 30m -> team lead; 60m -> platform manager; 3h -> engineering director.
- Communication: open incident channel in Slack #incidents and update the status page (status.redwood.com) for Sev-1 incidents.

9) Templates and code snippets
CI pipeline check for dashboards (example snippet):

cat > .github/workflows/validate-dashboard.yml <<'YAML'
name: Validate Grafana dashboard
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate-dashboard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: validate json schema
        run: grafana-dashboard-validator ./dashboards/$SERVICE.json
YAML

Alert rule example (Alertmanager annotations):
- alert: platform_platform_api_request_success_rate_low
  expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-api",env="prod"}[3m])) > 0) and (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-api",env="prod",code=~"5.."}[3m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-api",env="prod"}[3m]))) > 0.01
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "platform-api request success rate < 99.0% for 3m"
    runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/platform-api-runbook"

10) References and links
- Grafana template repo: git@github.com:redwood/grafana-templates.git
- Dashboard provisioning docs: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboard-provisioning

11) Change log
- 2026-01-20: Added p95 latency target guidance and new example PromQL queries.
- 2026-02-01: Adjusted alert thresholds for queue depth and added autoscaler stabilization to roadmap.
- 2026-03-01: Q4 addendum published (this document).

If you are a service owner and something in this playbook is out of date, please open a PR against this page and add yourself to reviewers. For guidance or help migrating dashboards/alerts, contact observability@redwood.com.
